video_directives: Diagram cards (gauge, 180dB, eardrum) hold long enough to register but the eardrum/crack beats could tighten by ~0.5s to keep the mid-section pressure
Character's reaction beats (dizzy X-eyes, wincing, shocked, sad) land well — add one more pose shift in the static 14-17s ship scene so the lower third never freezes
Loop closure is decent (erupting volcano echoes the hook composition) — hold the final card slightly longer with a settle-in ease instead of snapping to full frame

top3_directives: Push the volcano glow/crater rim with a brighter hotspot and subtle bloom so the eruption reads as the instant focal point at thumbnail size
Add a midground layer (islands, wave silhouettes, or distant mountains) between the glowing sky and the water band to create depth and kill the flat horizon seam
Tighten the text block's bottom margin and consider a warm accent word (e.g. 'LOUD' in ember orange) to tie the type palette to the crater glow
The '1883' pill floats ambiguously mid-air above the crater — anchor it with a small leader line or crater marker so the year clearly labels the volcano
The character's glow halo slightly bleeds into the JAVA label zone — either raise the label or dim the rim glow to keep the type crisp at small sizes
The large orange ring around the volcano is a second competing focal device — reduce its opacity ~20% or tighten it to the crater glow so the eye lands on the eruption first
Move the character sprite fully left or shrink it — its arm currently crowds the 'DO' and competes with the text block
Third caption line 'AGAIN.' reads slightly dimmer than lines 1-2; match stroke/gradient so all three lines carry equal weight in daylight
The horizon band transition from purple sky to navy sea cuts the volcano mid-slope — soften the seam or drop the character onto a cleaner ground plane
Merge the '180 dB' pill and 'PRESSURE WAVE' caption into ONE text system (e.g., 'PRESSURE WAVE — 180 dB') to eliminate the two-competing-blocks penalty
The bottom-right quadrant is near-empty — enlarge or reposition the pressure-wave rings to balance the character anchor bottom-left
Dim the gauge numerals (0/100/200) slightly or integrate them into the dial art so they stop reading as a second text layer
Resolve the harsh horizontal seam between the purple gradient panel and the dark lower band — blend them or use one continuous environment so the frame doesn't read as two glued screenshots
The red/blue swoosh entering the ear canal is ambiguous at Short size — replace with a clearer sound-wave glyph (concentric arcs) with a subtle glow so the 'loud sound entering ear' reads instantly

The suffering character is too dim and pushed into the corner with a large empty dark zone to its right — raise its luminance/rim light ~20% and either scale it up or pull it toward the lower third anchor point
Raise the character's brightness/outiline — it currently sinks into the dark navy water; add rim light or a subtle spotlight pool so the mascot reads on a 6-inch daylight screen
Resolve the focal conflict: ship silhouette and mascot compete for attention — either enlarge/center the ship as the hero or reposition the mascot out of the bottom-left corner dead zone
Unify the two text treatments (pill tag 'CRACK' + spaced caption 'EARDRUMS SPLIT') into one system with consistent casing, weight, and alignment to tighten the type hierarchy

Resolve the two competing text systems: integrate 'BOOM' into the scene as a styled impact/SFX element (distort, glow, or attach to the explosion arc) so only ONE text system (the caption pill) remains — currently it reads as a pasted-on headline
Activate the top third: the upper ~25% of frame is near-empty dead zone; extend the purple sky gradient texture, stars, or cloud layers upward to earn the vertical space

Lift the character off the dark lower panel: the navy hoodie melts into the navy background edge; add subtle rim light or local background warmth behind the figure for stronger foreground/background separation on a 6-inch daylight screen
The lower third is a near-black dead zone — the mascot is small, corner-pinned, and disconnected from the planet; either enlarge/integrate the character into the scene or crop the composition tighter
The cyan satellite dot and orbit ring compete subtly with the planet for focal attention — dim the ring or add a motion cue so the eye path is unambiguous
The caption bar sits awkwardly at the seam between the purple glow and black band — give it consistent breathing room and a subtle shadow so it doesn't feel pasted on
The '36,000 LIVES' line is cream-on-translucent-box over white wave foam — nearly invisible; give it a dark plate or heavy dark stroke
Upper ~35% of frame is a dead dark-purple void with a faint blob and moon — either push the composition up or add subtle depth/atmosphere there
The sad character is cropped against the frame edge and collides with the caption block zone — reposition fully inside frame with clear separation from text
Fill the top ~25% dead zone (stars only) with subtle atmosphere — clouds, aurora gradient, or rising embers connecting to the volcano glow

Enlarge or reposition the character so it doesn't fight the 'GONE.' header for focal attention — either scale it up toward lower-third center or add a subtle directional glow linking character → mountain
Give 'GONE.' a stronger separation plate (soft dark radial behind text) so its dark outline doesn't mush into the volcano tip and orange glow

Boost contrast on the 'CHILD OF KRAKATOA' subtitle line — dark type over the dark volcano silhouette will fail on a daylight phone screen; add a soft dark plate or brighten to the cream color used on the header chip

Fill or crop the upper ~35% dead sky zone — the character and volcano sit in the bottom half, leaving a large empty starfield; either scale the volcano/purple glow upward or push the label block higher

Resolve the dual focal point — the glowing mascot (bottom-left) and the volcano label compete; add an eye-path cue (character gesture line or light beam) connecting the mascot to the volcano, or dim the mascot glow
Character sits in bottom-left corner leaving lower-right third as a large dead zone — either enlarge the character or shift composition to rebalance the foreground
Orange arc/ring passes through the beam mid-frame creating a slightly muddy band; align the arc so its apex reads as a deliberate halo rather than slicing the focal beam
Character glow is soft but the dark sea and dark character outline nearly merge at the bottom edge; add a subtle rim light or horizon glow under the figure for separation
